job.title: Communications Specialist
job.description:
Looking for that elusive role that offers flexibility but also career fulfilment? This is a rare chance for a Communications Specialist to own the entire family lifecycle journey for one of Australia's fastest-growing, values-led early education groups, and to do it fully remotely or hybrid, full-time or part-time, with genuine flexibility around your life.

Reporting to the GM Marketing, Technology and Commercial and working alongside the Growth Office, you will bring a family engagement strategy to life across the full lifecycle. That means designing nurture journeys and lifecycle messaging for prospective, enrolled and existing families, building and optimising automations across Klaviyo, LineLeader and Owna, and developing content that drives occupancy, retention and advocacy. You will also partner with Centre Managers to showcase local stories and activations, and own the numbers, tracking open rates, click-throughs and engagement to keep improving what you ship.

You will bring at least three years in communications, marketing, or customer or community engagement, with real depth in building customer journeys and content across email, social and digital, plus hands-on experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms. Sharp writing, confident stakeholder management and the composure to juggle multiple campaigns are essential. Experience in childcare, education or community organisations will set you apart. The people who thrive here are warm and empathetic, but also organised, self-directed and commercially minded.

This is a purpose-driven, community-focused organisation where communication is treated as core to growth, and where your work has visible impact on real families and centres. The option is there to work in whatever way suits your lifestyle, either 4 days a week or full time, hybrid or remote (on the east coast).

If you want to own the lifecycle journey end to end and see your communication translate directly into business growth, this is the role to apply for.

job.title: Key Account Manager
job.description:
Work with a global leader in Consumer Health whose portfolio includes some of the country's most trusted brands.

The Key Account Manager owns the partnership with one of Australia's two major grocery retailers. It's a genuinely commercial, reporting to the National Business Manager, Grocery. You'll set the growth agenda, shape the investment strategy, and build the relationships that make it all happen.

Day to day, you'll own the annual customer growth plan and deliver on sales, profit, market share and investment targets. That means leading the forecasting, joint business planning and commercial reviews, managing trade investment and profitability, and applying Revenue Growth Management principles to sharpen ROI. You'll spot new growth through customer, category and shopper insights, and work across Sales, Marketing, Category, Finance, Supply Chain and Trade Activation to get it executed well.

This one suits people currently in FMCG or Consumer Health account management, or coming across from a competitor. You'll have at least 3 years managing customer accounts, ideally with major retailers or banner groups, plus strong commercial acumen across trade investment and promotional effectiveness. You're analytical, comfortable turning data into action, and hands-on with tools like Circana/IRI, Nielsen, Quantium or Power BI. Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder skills round it out.

With a strong package and car allowance, a wonderful opportunity to work with incredible brands.

job.title: National Business Manager, Grocery
job.description:
A senior leadership role with a global Consumer Health business, owning the Grocery, Independent Grocery and eCommerce channels and the growth behind them.

You'll set the direction across all three channels and carry the commercial performance, leading the growth strategies that move sales, profitability, market share and category position. Annual planning, forecasting and performance management sit with you, along with the customer growth plans, joint business planning and commercial agreements you'll negotiate with major retailers, independent groups and eCommerce partners. Much of it is done through influence, bringing customer teams together and working across Sales, Marketing, Category, Finance and Supply Chain to get priorities delivered. Category and shopper insight is your starting point for where pricing, promotional investment, assortment and trade spend go to earn the best return.

We're keen to hear from people coming across from a competitor or elsewhere in FMCG. You'll have five or more years managing major customers, channels or commercial portfolios, with a clear record of building growth strategies that landed. A strong grasp of trade investment, profitability, gross-to-net and ROI matters, along with real depth in grocery retail and category management, and you'll be at ease reading data through platforms like Circana, Nielsen, Quantium or Power BI. You'll also have led well inside a matrix, influencing senior stakeholders and driving alignment.
